title: Day 3 Activity and Assignment
summary: Role-play a misunderstanding between two staff members and show a better communication approach, then practise active listening on the floor and write one example.

items.label: Focus
items.body: Clear speech, active listening, asking questions and reporting to the right person

sections.title: Activity: Role-play a misunderstanding
paragraphs: Work in pairs. One person is Staff A and the other is Staff B.
First, act the situation as it often goes wrong: interrupting, assuming, rude words, or complaining to the wrong person.
Then replay the same situation using a better approach from Day 3: listen fully, ask a clarifying question, confirm the instruction, and speak politely.
A third person may observe and say what changed.
Use one of the scenes below, or a similar work situation. Do not name real colleagues.

sections.title: Scene 1 — The interrupted booking change
paragraphs: A receptionist starts to explain that a client has requested a change. The therapist interrupts: "I can't take another client!" The receptionist was only trying to say the client wants to move the appointment to another day.
list: What did interruption cause?
What question would have prevented the assumption?
Replay: listen to the full message, then confirm what the client wants.

sections.title: Scene 2 — "Prepare the room"
paragraphs: A supervisor says: "Please prepare the room for the next client." The therapist arranges the massage bed and leaves. Towels and supplies are not ready. The therapist says: "You didn't tell me everything."
list: What was missing from the instruction?
What should the therapist have asked?
Replay: give a specific instruction, confirm understanding, and report when the room is ready.

sections.title: Scene 3 — The air conditioner complaint
paragraphs: A therapist notices Room 2 is not cooling. She complains to several colleagues. Nobody tells a supervisor. A client later complains about the temperature.
list: Who should have received the concern?
What facts should the report include?
Replay: report clearly to the right person and ask whether another room should be used.

sections.title: Scene 4 — The WhatsApp argument
paragraphs: Two employees disagree in the staff WhatsApp group about who was supposed to prepare a room. The messages become personal. Other staff join in.
list: Why is the group the wrong place for this?
What would a professional message sound like?
Replay: state the fact, confirm who is responsible, and move any personal disagreement off the group.

sections.title: After the role-play
list: Which words made the first version worse?
Did anyone listen without interrupting?
Was a clarifying question asked?
Was the concern sent to someone who could act?
What would you do differently on a real shift?

sections.title: Assignment: Practise active listening
paragraphs: During your next shift, practise active listening in a real work conversation.
Choose one situation: a client preference, a colleague's explanation, a supervisor's instruction, or a booking update.
Do not interrupt unless safety requires it. Ask a clarifying question if needed. Confirm what you understood. Then follow through.
Write down one situation where listening improved communication.

sections.title: How to complete the assignment
list: Situation: What was being communicated, and by whom? (No gossip or private details.)
What I might have assumed if I had not listened.
What I did: attention, no unnecessary interruption, question, confirmation.
How it improved the outcome for the client, colleague or team.
One listening habit I will keep using.

remember: A misunderstanding often starts with interruption or assumption. Listen fully, ask, confirm, then act. Practise that on the floor and write one example.
